title: The water cycle: practice
description: Six ways to answer, one topic.

questions.prompt: Water vapour cools and turns back into liquid droplets in a process called ___. When the droplets grow heavy they fall as ___.
questions.hint: The first word is the opposite of evaporation.
questions.explanation: Condensation forms clouds; precipitation returns the water to the ground.

questions.prompt: Roughly what percentage of Earth's water is fresh water?
questions.explanation: About 2.5–3%, and most of that is frozen in ice caps and glaciers.

questions.prompt: Put the stages of the water cycle in order, starting from the ocean.

items.text: Runoff back to rivers and the sea

questions.prompt: Is each one a source of water vapour, or a way water returns to the ground?
Why does the water cycle need energy from the Sun?
questions.rubric: • The Sun heats water so it evaporates. • Evaporation needs energy (latent heat). • Without it, water wouldn't rise into the atmosphere.
questions.sample: The Sun's heat gives water molecules the energy to evaporate and rise as vapour; without that energy the cycle couldn't lift water into the air.

questions.prompt: Which process moves water from plants into the air?

options.rationale: Plants release water vapour through their leaves.
That's water soaking into the ground.
